{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish and drew the full sketch on the pad in the first minute, so the table had a clear plan and a shape that works as a domino picture: a big left-facing fish with a swooshy tail, built from smooth curves. I laid the start domino and the long top line from the tail round toward the nose, which every other piece hangs off. I also carried the bottom line from the belly toward the tail. By the time of the push, about 116 of the 119 standing dominoes were connected to the start.

Execution: I traced the strokes from the pad, which kept the outline clean and the curves gentle enough for the fall to pass. I inspected the top line and the tail section, and I spotted a jammed domino near the tail tip and flagged it so it was fixed before the push. I kept my hands off the finished work in the last minutes so nothing got bumped.

Collaboration: I gave clear, specific hand-offs. Maya took the bottom line, Tom took the top line round the nose and later the tail tip, and Leo checked the joins. I told people where to work so we stayed out of each other's way and avoided bumps. I kept the table updated on progress and on what was still needed.

Leadership: I set the direction early, picked the animal, and assigned the strokes. I called time checks and the final hands-off so the table stopped building and let the push run cleanly. I kept the mood light and the table focused through the last two minutes.", "my_share_percent": 40}
